<reason>Both sides built genuinely strong cases, but A's central distinguishing argument — that bankruptcy discharge is a one-time, irreversible write-off at the borrower's earnings trough that lets her keep all future upside, whereas IBR forgiveness is preceded by decades of continuous income monitoring and clawback if earnings rise — survived the exchange essentially intact. B's strongest counter (that both systems produce the "same" fiscal write-off, so bankruptcy is just IBR without the cruelty) never squarely answered what happens to post-discharge income growth; B's closing restates that the borrower "isn't eligible" if income rises, but this conflates the ex-ante discharge test with the absence of any ex-post clawback mechanism once discharge is granted, which was exactly A's point. A's related arguments — access effects on future marginal borrowers, and moral hazard reframed as rational multi-year underemployment rather than immediate discharge — were pressed consistently and never fully neutralized. B landed real hits (the "cruelty vs. pricing" reframe, turning the administrability objection back on disability/support systems, and a concrete 15-20 year verified-income standard in response to pressure), and its pressure questions were sharp and created real tension for A to resolve. But B's case suffered an execution cost: both the opening and first rebuttal were clipped for exceeding word limits, denying the reader some of B's development, while A stayed within limits throughout and used the space efficiently. On balance, A's case was more resilient at the point of final clash and better executed procedurally, giving it a clear but not dominant edge.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>The exchange over IBR vs. bankruptcy discharge (A2.3/A4.1-2 vs B2.2/B4.2/B5.1) was decisive: A's reversibility/upside-retention distinction was pressed repeatedly and never cleanly answered, while B's "identical write-off, just crueler" reframe was rhetorically strong but left the post-discharge clawback asymmetry unresolved.</best_rebuttal>
